study_identification_part.si4_title: Cortical thickness deviations as biomarker for subtyping and prognosis in pediatric brainstem tumors

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: This study investigates whole-brain structural alterations in pediatric brainstem tumor patients through cortical thickness (CTh) analysis, aiming to identify subtype-specific CTh patterns as non-invasive biomarkers for patient stratification and evaluate the prognostic value of CTh deviations in predicting overall survival.

rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.supporting_text: For each individual, CTh was calculated using the CAT12 toolbox (version 12.7). The procedure involved segmenting MRI data to distinguish gray matter, white matter, and cerebrospinal fluid. Then, the pial surface and gray matter/white matter boundary were reconstructed, and CTh was measured as the distance between the corresponding vertices. The cortex was parcellated into 210 distinct regions using the Human Brainnetome Atlas, and the mean CTh for each region was calculated.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Statistical analyses included Mann-Whitney U tests and Kruskal-Wallis tests for comparing continuous variables (tOCN-CT, tOCP-CT, tumor volume, OS) across groups, with Dunn's post-hoc tests for pairwise comparisons. ANCOVA was used for categorical variables with age as a covariate. Two-way ANCOVA evaluated interaction effects of tumor growth patterns and subtypes on clinical factors. Spectral clustering (Scikit-learn) was applied to CTh deviation maps to identify patient subtypes, with the optimal number of clusters determined by Calinski-Harabasz Scores. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis with log-rank tests assessed survival differences between subtypes. Cox proportional hazards models (univariate and multivariate) identified prognostic factors. Partial correlation analysis examined relationships between tumor volume and CTh deviations. Two-sample t-tests with FDR correction compared CTh deviations between subtypes. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05 (two-tailed). Key findings: Subtype 2 showed significantly better survival than Subtype 1 (p=0.02, Cohen's d=0.61); focal tumors associated with more tOCN-CT than diffuse tumors (F=12.63, p=0.0005); tumor volume positively correlated with tOCP-CT (partial r=0.17, p=0.047); tOCN-CT correlated with OS (r=0.44, p=0.001); multivariate Cox regression identified longer symptom duration as protective (coef=-0.08, p=0.01) and diffuse tumor growth as trending toward worse prognosis (coef=0.66, p=0.05).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Two distinct patient subtypes were identified based on cortical thickness deviations (Subtype 1 with positive deviations, Subtype 2 with negative deviations), with Subtype 2 showing significantly better survival outcomes (p=0.02), and cortical thickness patterns correlating with tumor growth patterns and volumes.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: This study of 145 pediatric brainstem tumor patients and 849 healthy controls identified two distinct patient subtypes using spectral clustering of cortical thickness (CTh) deviations. Subtype 1 (n=100) exhibited widespread positive CTh deviations predominantly in postcentral gyrus, temporal pole, middle frontal gyrus, and superior parietal lobule. Subtype 2 (n=45) demonstrated extensive negative deviations primarily in temporoparietal junction, inferior frontal gyrus, and inferior temporal gyrus. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis revealed significantly better survival probability for Subtype 2 compared to Subtype 1 (p=0.02, Cohen's d=0.61). Focal tumors (n=31) were significantly associated with more negative CTh deviations (tOCN-CT) than diffuse tumors (n=114; F=12.63, p=0.0005). Tumor volume positively correlated with positive CTh deviations (tOCP-CT; partial r=0.17, p=0.047), and tOCN-CT correlated with overall survival (r=0.44, p=0.001). Multivariate Cox regression identified longer symptom duration as an independent protective factor (coef=-0.08, 95% CI: -0.02-0.87, p=0.01), while diffuse tumor growth pattern trended toward worse prognosis (coef=0.66, 95% CI: -0.02-0.87, p=0.05). Over 25% of patients had extreme deviations in at least five brain regions, with 13% showing persistent cortical thinning across multiple regions. The study demonstrates that CTh deviations serve as non-invasive imaging markers for patient subtyping and survival prediction in pediatric brainstem tumors.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Validation in larger multi-center cohorts needed; cross-sectional design limits causal inference; molecular/genomic data not integrated; impact of treatment modalities not systematically analyzed; multimodal imaging biomarkers not incorporated; longitudinal assessment of CTh changes over time lacking
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: However, this study has several limitations that warrant further investigation. First, these findings need validation in more extensive, multi-center cohorts to ensure their generalizability across different populations and healthcare settings... Second, while this study focuses on CTh deviations, it does not account for genomic alteration or proteomic signature, which are critical drivers of tumor aggressiveness and treatment resistance... Third, the cross-sectional design limits the ability to establish causal relationships between CTh deviations and clinical outcomes. Longitudinal studies are needed to assess the dynamic changes in CTh over time and their associations with disease progression, treatment response, and long-term survival. Fourth, while we adjusted for age as a covariate, the impact of treatment modalities (e.g., surgical resection extent, chemotherapy regimens) on disease duration and OS was not systematically analyzed, potentially confounding prognostic interpretations.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Spectral clustering was used for unsupervised patient subtyping based on cortical thickness deviation maps, with the optimal number of clusters determined by Calinski-Harabasz scores. The study computed region-specific extreme deviation rates (proportion of patients with |Z|>1.96 in each region) to identify anatomically specific patterns. Two-way ANCOVA was employed to assess interaction effects between tumor subtype and growth pattern on clinical outcomes. The study used Human Brainnetome Atlas (210 regions) for parcellation, providing fine-grained anatomical specificity. Manual tumor segmentation was performed using MRIcronGL and validated by two neurosurgical experts. Age was adjusted as a covariate in all intergroup comparisons, survival analyses, and Cox regressions due to its known confounding effects. The study highlights that CTh evaluation could serve as a preoperative prognostic biomarker supporting personalized treatment strategies.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: The study includes a subset of 57 patients with sufficient longitudinal follow-up for overall survival analysis out of the total 145 patients. The main clinical endpoint was overall survival (OS), defined as days from initial pathological diagnosis to death or last known alive date. The study excluded patients with severe cerebellar compression or poor image quality. The paper was previously published as a preprint on bioRxiv but has undergone substantial revisions including updated title, figures, and expanded results. Tumor features (location, growth pattern, volume) were assessed through MRI, with tumor volumes manually delineated and calculated from voxel counts. H3K27M mutation status was assessed but showed no significant differences in CTh deviations between wildtype and mutant groups (Supplementary Fig. 1). The study found age-related effects on symptoms (nausea: U=1693, p=0.04; dysarthria: U=1343, p=0.005) and on tOCP-CT (partial r=-0.36, p<0.005). The normative model was validated using 10-fold cross-validation before finalizing. ComBat harmonization was applied across three datasets (note: text mentions four source databases but three datasets for harmonization). The study demonstrates that brainstem tumors exert distant effects on cortical organization, with both cortical thickening and thinning observed depending on tumor characteristics. IRB approval: Beijing Tiantan Hospital (Approval No. KY 2019-124-02); conducted per 1964 Helsinki Declaration.
